title: Two-dimensional weak-interface supershear convergence contract
purpose: Require the supershear mechanism, energy closure, and fitted front speed to survive proportional in-plane mesh refinement and explicit time-step refinement.
physics: near-incompressible finite-strain plane-stress Neo-Hookean strip with ten or more cells through the height, homogeneous preload, smooth remote impact, a fixed bilinear Mode-I cohesive interface, and a precrack

execution.evidence: The opt-in public benchmark compares a 30x10 baseline, a near-proportional 40x14 spatial refinement, and a 30x10 run with the stable time increment halved. It is kept outside per-commit CI because the complete local run takes several minutes.

observables: Resolved supershear classification and fitted speed normalized by the prestrained reference-coordinate shear speed.
Interface and transverse cell counts, stable time increment, simultaneous failure fraction, and rapid distributed-failure fraction.
Complete bulk, kinetic, cohesive, prescribed-work, and energy-balance ledger at retained frames.
Relative fitted-speed changes under proportional spatial refinement and time-step halving.
acceptance: All three runs remain supershear with fewer than ten percent of intact facets failing in one increment.
Every run closes the complete energy ledger within 0.5 percent.
The 30x10 to 40x14 fitted-speed change remains below ten percent.
Halving the 30x10 time increment changes fitted speed by less than two percent.
limitations: The accepted contract establishes two-dimensional mechanism convergence, not publication-parameter or curve-level reproduction.
The spatial speed difference is about seven percent; a third proportional mesh remains necessary for an asymptotic convergence-rate claim.
The local plane-stress membrane still requires a thin-three-dimensional cross-check and an independent near-incompressibility study.
The V4 interface is normally preloaded and therefore cannot use the traction-free principal surface-wave oracle as a prestrained Rayleigh boundary.
